limits: Only the two Latin forms the rule names. 'etc.,' is left alone: a comma after 'etc.' is often correct punctuation of the sentence around it.

statement: Don't use commas with Latin shortened forms

density_justification: dates-and-time.md shows three ISO 8601 basic-format strings (2023007, 23007, 153020) as examples of that format. They are identifiers, which the rule does not govern.
limits: Catches digits grouped with spaces ('6 500', the manual's own Not this) and runs of 5 or more digits. A bare 4-digit count ('6500 complaints') is not caught: telling it from a year or a postcode needs meaning, so that half is Tier 1 (the reviewer's note says as much). Phone numbers, standards codes and 8-digit dates are excluded.
proposed_by: drafted by Claude (model) on 2026-09-23; declarative data, adopted only by a named human (D-10)
statement: Use commas in numbers with 4 or more digits

limits: The coordinated-subject case ('My colleague and myself travelled'), where a verb follows. A reflexive alone as subject ('Myself will attend') is rare and not caught.
proposed_by: drafted by Claude (model) on 2026-09-23; declarative data, adopted only by a named human (D-10)
statement: Don't use reflexive pronouns such as 'yourself' and 'myself' as the subject of the verb.

limits: A sentence-opening prepositional phrase that ends in a numeral and is followed by a comma and another numeral. An opening that is not a prepositional phrase is not caught; requiring one is what stops it firing on lists such as 'sections 4, 5 and 7'.
proposed_by: drafted by Claude (model) on 2026-09-23; declarative data, adopted only by a named human (D-10)
statement: Avoid beginning a sentence with a string of numbers and dates

density_justification: The manual itself leaves out the comma four times (alt-text, journals, pronouns, classics). Those are real lapses by the letter of the rule, and a correct rule is expected to fire a handful of times (ADR-011).
limits: No comma before 'for example' after a word, or none after it before a lowercase word. 'for example ‘X’' and a trailing 'for example.' are not flagged: the manual uses both throughout, and the rule's own condition exempts a colon.
proposed_by: drafted by Claude (model) on 2026-09-23; declarative data, adopted only by a named human (D-10)
statement: Use commas with the phrase 'for example'

limits: Negative tags only ('…, won’t we?'). Positive tags ('…, are they?') are left to Tier 1, because 'is it?' ends ordinary questions too. A parenthetical 'why wouldn’t they?' is excluded.
proposed_by: drafted by Claude (model) on 2026-09-23; declarative data, adopted only by a named human (D-10)
statement: Separate questions tagged onto a sentence

density_justification: Six mentions and scientific notation: measurement-and-units.md tabulates SI multiples (1,000,000 and up) and converts '63 megalitres is 63,000,000 litres'; choosing-numerals-or-words.md writes '2.5 × 10⁶ is the same as 2,500,000'; an editor's tip contrasts '1 million' with '1,000,000'.
limits: A million or more written in full and rounded to the hundred thousand ('2,500,000', '1,000,000'). '1,250,000' is left alone, and so is anything under a million. Quoted mentions are skipped, so the numbers page's own ‘2.5 million’ than ‘2,500,000’ does not fire.
proposed_by: drafted by Claude (model) on 2026-09-23; declarative data, adopted only by a named human (D-10)
statement: Use numerals and words for large, rounded numbers

limits: A speech verb followed directly by an opening quote with no comma. 'wrote' is excluded: quoted verse and text after 'wrote' take no comma in the manual's own citations.
proposed_by: drafted by Claude (model) on 2026-09-23; declarative data, adopted only by a named human (D-10)
statement: Show direct speech or quoted material using commas

limits: Terms in single quotes are mentions and are skipped, which is why the manual's own 'Don’t use the term ‘old people’' does not fire. 'elderly' alone is left out: it is also an adjective the manual uses in quotations.
